gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the one maker weight below 1.3 lb for a lid-attached screen, Xebec's "1lb per screen" for the Snap, leaves out the Snap Bracket the screen hangs from (1.5 lb in Xebec's spec list), which puts one mounted Snap screen at about 2.5 lb and over the 2 lb line.
standout_why: I compared four pages. PCWorld Shop's Duex Lite page (cited) gives only "Weight: 1.3lbs" plus box contents. thedadsneeze.com (rank 12) gives 1.3 lb and 1.8 lb for the two Duex DS sizes without saying what the figures include. Mobile Pixels' own travel blog tables 1.3 lb as a maker-stated figure with no inclusion note. Xebec's Snap pages carry "1lb" and "1.5 lb" in one unlabelled spec list and never add them. ChatGPT's answer itself said it could not establish that 1.3 lb is the market minimum; this finding closes that. It is not a 3 because it confirms the pick rather than changing it, and Xebec's own page holds the raw numbers. The cited mobilepixels.us Duex DS product and collection pages returned HTTP 429 on every attempt today, so I could not compare against them directly.
decides: It confirms the Mobile Pixels Duex Plus DS (ours, 1.3 lb maker-stated) as the lightest attached extender under 2 lb. The only lower maker figure found, Xebec Snap at 1 lb, is per screen without its bracket; with the bracket it is about 2.5 lb and uses a DisplayLink chip, so it belongs in the left-out list beside the Tri-Screen 2. The Duex Lite 12.5" is listed at the same 1.3 lb, so the smaller screen saves no weight. The table footnote should say that every weight in it is the screen alone as the maker states it, and that no maker read today gives a figure including magnets, mount or cables.

findings.label: Maker-stated weight, and what it covers
findings.source_title: What are the Snap Screen tech specs? (Xebec help center)
findings.note: The page says "1lb per screen" for a 13.3" 1920×1080 screen, 12.4" × 7.4" × 0.33", up to 400 nits, for laptops 13 to 17.5 inches (Xebec's range), and says a USB-A or USB-C port is required. It does not mention the bracket. The page shows only "Updated 5 months ago".

findings.label: Snap Bracket weight (the mount the screen attaches to)
findings.note: The spec list gives 1.5 lb alongside the bracket's other specs (225° range of motion, pass-through charging, 2 integrated USB-C cables), but the list is not clearly labelled, so the attribution to the bracket is a reading of the layout. The page says "With the included Snap Bracket, easily attach up to two pieces of Snap Gear to your laptop."

findings.label: Normalised weight on the laptop: one screen plus bracket
findings.value: about 2.5 lb (two screens plus bracket: about 3.5 lb)
findings.note: Arithmetic on Xebec's own figures: 1 lb screen + 1.5 lb bracket = 2.5 lb; 2 × 1 lb + 1.5 lb = 3.5 lb. Cables are not counted. This holds only if the 1.5 lb line is the bracket (see the previous finding). Either way the mounted Snap is over the 2 lb line.

findings.label: Video path
findings.value: DisplayLink 6000-series chip; connection over USB-A needs the free DisplayLink driver
findings.note: Xebec's wording: "Connection via USB-A requires the free DisplayLink driver download." The page lists Windows, Mac, Chromebook and Linux. It does not state a native USB-C DisplayPort Alt Mode path.

findings.label: Price at Xebec's US store
findings.note: Black Friday strike-through pricing. The page does not say how many screens the $529 starting configuration includes, and no sale end date was read.

findings.label: Maker-stated weight
findings.source_title: How do I choose a portable monitor for frequent travel? (Mobile Pixels blog, Jime Chen, 2026-10-18)
findings.note: From the table headed "Manufacturer-Stated Weights of Popular Portable Monitors (lb)". Conversion: 1.3 × 453.6 g = 590 g. The article does not say whether the figure counts the lid magnets or the cable, and it advises "Weigh your whole kit, not just the monitor". The same table lists Fold 15.6" at 1.65 lb, Duex Float 2 Pro at 2.9 lb and Trio 3 Pro at 4.13 lb.

findings.label: Listed weight and what ships beside the screen
findings.value: 1.3 lb; box adds one USB-C cable, one HDMI cable with USB-C adapter, 8 nano-adhesive tape pieces, 4 magnetic adhesive pieces
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Duex Lite: Portable Dual-Screen Laptop Monitor (Green) | PCWorld Shop
findings.note: This is a retailer page reprinting the spec ("Weight: 1.3lbs", 12.4" × 8.45" × 0.39"), not the maker's page. The weight line sits apart from the box list, so the magnets and cables are extra and unweighed. Price on the page was $139.99. For laptops without USB-C the page notes "Driver required".

findings.label: Weight as reprinted by a named reviewer
findings.source_title: SideTrak Swivel FHD 14" attached portable monitor review (The Gadgeteer, Howard Sneider, 2024-01-01)
findings.note: This is the spec list in the review, not a scale reading, and it does not say whether the metal mounting plates are counted. Sneider writes that the included kickstand "can help on lighter-weight laptops which may fall backwards with the weight of the external monitor". The review is of a 2024 unit; the current model and price were not read.

findings.label: What rival round-ups do with these weights
findings.value: Duex Plus DS 1.3 lb and Duex Max DS 1.8 lb, with no note on what the figures include
findings.source_title: Best Laptop Screen Extender (2026): 7 Picks From $90
findings.note: The page was used for the rival comparison only. It is not a maker source for the Duex Max DS's 1.8 lb.

Weight of the four lid magnets or adhesive plates for any Duex model: no page opened gives it, so a true "weight added to the lid" figure for the Duex Plus DS could not be built.

Xebec Snap Bracket product page (thexebec.com/products/xebec-snap-bracket), for an explicitly labelled bracket weight, its price and the statement that it is required for the Snap Screen: HTTP 429. The $129 price and "required" wording appeared only in a search summary.
